audit.reasoning: Quote: we held no file; I downloaded the cited Waikato thesis (open, hdl 10289/5755), scanned the cited pages, and the deciding sentence is verbatim on p.51 sec 3.3, with pp.53-54 reinforcing strict initial stress (prefixes take the stress; non-phonemic). Deciding source is a 2010 MA-thesis grammar sketch, the top Glottolog item, fieldwork-based but impressionistic and register-blind. Web search found the one dedicated prosodic study, Heinz 2004 (UCLA MA thesis, open), now downloaded: it confirms initial main stress for the Normal (everyday spoken) register ('main stress always falls on the initial syllable', p.31) but describes the Citation register as penult-plus-alternating-leftward with main stress on the leftmost stressed syllable and CVV syllables attracting stress (pp.13-15), i.e. odd-parity all-light words would carry main stress on the second syllable in careful/citation speech. sources.quote: Normal register: 'Unlike the Citation form, in the Normal form, main stress always falls on the initial syllable' (p.31); 'Main stress is on the initial syllable, and heavy syllables bear stress, except when following an initial light syllable' (p.32). Citation register: 'Stress in the Citation form is rhythmic; generally, secondary stress falls on the penultimate and alternating syllables leftward. sources.note: Only dedicated phonological study of Kwara'ae prosody; splits stress by register (Normal: initial main stress; Citation: penult-plus-alternating with main stress leftmost, CVV attracts stress) which Macdonald's 3-page section does not; should be added as second source and the register caveat noted.
